stimulus.text: Martin Waldseemuller's world map, published in 1507, was the first map to use the name America for the lands across the Atlantic Ocean. It shows the western lands as a separate landmass. The portrait of Amerigo Vespucci stands beside one globe at the top of the map, and the portrait of the ancient geographer Ptolemy stands beside the other globe.
stimulus.source_note: Waldseemuller map, 1507, public domain; Library of Congress.

stem: What change in European knowledge does the 1507 map best show?

options.text: Europeans recognized the western lands as a separate continent, not part of Asia.
Europeans had fully charted the Pacific coast of the Americas by 1507.
The map proves that Columbus had reached Asia on his voyages.
The map leaves Africa off the world entirely, showing no African coast.

instruction: Pick one option from the stimulus and stem only. Do not open the question file.
